title: Treatment and care words
blurb: Know the HESI A2 words for the goal of care, procedures and recovery, and never mix up palliative and prophylactic or incision and excision.
question: A care plan says a patient will receive palliative care, a prophylactic antibiotic and wound debridement. Which of these is meant to prevent a problem, which only eases symptoms, and which removes something?

teach.body: Formally, treatment and care words describe the purpose, method and stage of medical care: whether it prevents, cures or comforts, how it is done, and how the patient recovers. In plain English: each word answers 'what is this care trying to do?' On the HESI A2 the wrong options are usually the neighboring goal (prevent instead of comfort) or a look-alike word (incision for excision), so learn the words in sets.

teach.h: Scenario: Keisha reads a discharge plan
teach.body: Keisha Brown, a CNA applying to an RN program, reads: 'Elective hernia repair. Incision closed with sutures; keep the dressing dry. Ambulate three times a day. Convalescence about two weeks.' She translates: the surgery was scheduled, not urgent; the surgical cut was stitched; the wound covering stays dry; walk three times a day; expect two weeks of gradual recovery. No tissue was removed for testing, so 'excision' would have been the wrong word.

teach.text: Classic swaps: incision (cut into) vs excision (cut out); palliative (comfort) vs prophylactic (prevent); regimen (care plan) vs regiment (military unit); alleviate (ease) vs elevate (raise); ambulate (walk) vs amputate (cut off). Also beware the option that fits the sentence but is not the word's meaning.

items: Cover the options and say what the word means in your own words.
Check the word parts: ex- = out, in- = into, pro- = before, re- = again.
Read the sentence to confirm the sense, but do not pick the option that only fits the topic.
Cross out the look-alike and the opposite, then choose.
Prophylactic prevents, therapeutic treats, curative cures, palliative eases symptoms.
Alleviate, mitigate and ameliorate all mean make better or less severe; exacerbate means make worse.
Incision = cut into; excision = cut out; suture = stitch; debridement = remove dead tissue.
Triage = sort by urgency; regimen = care plan; protocol = official steps; adjunct = add-on support.
Convalescence = recovery period; rehabilitation = restoring ability; ambulate = walk.

summary: You can now name the goal of care (prophylactic, therapeutic, curative, palliative) and read the procedure and recovery words on a care plan. You can also spot the look-alikes the HESI A2 uses as distractors, such as incision and excision or regimen and regiment.

A.q: The surgeon made a small incision just below the patient's navel. What is the best definition of the word "incision" in this sentence?
options: a cut made with a blade
a stitch to close the skin
a tube placed to drain fluid
A.why: An incision is a cut made with a blade, as in surgery (in- = into, cis = cut).

whyNot.1: Removing tissue is excision, the classic incision look-alike.
whyNot.3: A drainage tube fits surgery loosely, but it is not the meaning of incision.

A.q: Antibiotics are curative for most cases of strep throat. What is the best definition of the word "curative" in this sentence?
A.why: Curative means able to cure: the antibiotic clears the infection.

whyNot.0: Easing symptoms without curing is palliative.
whyNot.3: Building up over time is cumulative, a look-alike word.

A.q: Which word means "to keep from moving"?
A.why: Immobilize means to keep from moving (im- = not, mobil = movable), as a splint does.

whyNot.0: Mobilize means to make movable, the opposite.
whyNot.1: Immunize means to make immune; it only looks like immobilize.

B.q: Mrs. Patel will need weeks of rehabilitation after her stroke. What is the best definition of the word "rehabilitation" in this sentence?
options: a long stay in a nursing home
B.why: Rehabilitation is restoring health or ability after illness or injury.

whyNot.0: Replacing fluids is rehydration, a look-alike word.
whyNot.2: Rehab may happen in a facility, but the word means restoring ability, not the place.
whyNot.3: Supervision fits the sentence loosely, but it is not the meaning of rehabilitation.

B.q: The nurse documented each intervention she used to bring down the patient's fever. What is the best definition of the word "intervention" in this sentence?
options: a talk held with the family
a goal set for the day
B.why: An intervention is an action taken to improve a situation or condition, such as a cool cloth for a fever.

whyNot.0: Taking a reading is a measurement; it fits documentation loosely but is not an intervention.
whyNot.1: A talk is an interaction, a look-alike word.
whyNot.3: A goal is what the care aims for, not the action itself.

B.q: Brianna's knee surgery is elective, so she booked it for her winter break. What is the best definition of the word "elective" in this sentence?
B.why: Elective means chosen or scheduled; not an emergency.

whyNot.1: Needed right away is emergent, the opposite.
whyNot.2: Outpatient care is ambulatory; elective is about urgency, not overnight stays.
whyNot.3: Payment fits the sentence loosely, but elective describes timing and choice.

C.q: Paramedics worked for twenty minutes to resuscitate the man pulled from the lake. What is the best definition of the word "resuscitate" in this sentence?
C.why: Resuscitate means to revive someone from unconsciousness or apparent death.

whyNot.0: Rewarming may be part of the care after cold water, but it is not the meaning of resuscitate.
whyNot.1: Transport fits the scene loosely; resuscitate means to bring back to consciousness.
whyNot.2: Restrain means to hold back; it is not related.

C.q: After two days of bed rest, Mr. Young began to recuperate from the flu. What is the best definition of the word "recuperate" in this sentence?
C.why: Recuperate means to recover health or strength.

whyNot.0: Falling ill again is relapse, the opposite.
whyNot.3: Sleep fits the bed-rest setting loosely, but recuperate means to recover.

C.q: Which pair of words have opposite meanings?
C.why: Alleviate means to make less severe; exacerbate means to make worse.

whyNot.0: Mitigate and alleviate both mean to make less severe.
whyNot.1: Ameliorate means to improve, so these are synonyms.
whyNot.3: Palliative care soothes symptoms, so these are close in meaning.

reteach.title: Treatment words as roof repairs
reteach.question: If a storm damages your roof, how could you prevent, patch, fix or just live with the leak? How do those choices map onto treatment words?

blocks.body: Sealing the roof before the storm season is prophylactic: it prevents the problem. A bucket under the drip is palliative: the leak stays, but the mess is eased. Replacing the broken shingles is curative: the leak is gone. Tearing out the rotten wood first is debridement. A tarp tied over the new shingles is an adjunct: extra support for the main repair.

blocks.text: The bucket helps a lot, but it never fixes the roof. Palliative care can be excellent care, yet its goal is comfort, not cure.

explain.body: Prophylactic = prevent (before illness). Therapeutic = treat or heal. Curative = cure. Palliative = ease symptoms without curing.

steps.label: palliative
steps.sub: comfort when cure is not the aim

test.q: Which word describes care meant to prevent a disease before it develops?

whyNot.0: Palliative care eases symptoms without curing.
whyNot.2: Therapeutic care treats an existing condition.
whyNot.3: Curative care cures an existing disease.

explain.body: Alleviate, mitigate and ameliorate all move a problem toward better. Exacerbate and aggravate move it toward worse. Watch the look-alikes: elevate, migrate, deteriorate.

test.q: Which word means "to make pain less severe"?
test.why: Alleviate means to make pain or a problem less severe.

whyNot.0: Elevate means to raise; it only looks like alleviate.
whyNot.2: Exacerbate means to make worse, the opposite.

explain.body: Incision = a cut into tissue. Excision = cutting tissue out. Suture = a stitch. Dressing = a wound covering. Debridement = removing dead tissue. Invasive = entering the body.

test.q: After the procedure, the nurse placed a sterile dressing over the wound. What is the best definition of the word "dressing" in this sentence?
test.why: A dressing is a covering applied to a wound.

whyNot.1: A cleaning solution is used before the dressing; it is not the dressing.
whyNot.3: A tube that removes fluid is a drain.

explain.body: Regimen = a prescribed plan. Protocol = official steps. Triage = sorting by urgency. Convalescence = recovery period. Rehabilitation = restoring ability. Ambulate = walk.

test.q: Which word means "a prescribed plan of diet, exercise or medication"?
test.why: A regimen is a prescribed plan of diet, exercise or medication.

whyNot.0: A regiment is a military unit; it differs from regimen by one letter.
whyNot.1: A specimen is a sample taken for testing.
whyNot.3: A requisition is a written request, such as an order for supplies or a lab test.
